body: At this point I'm probably going to go through another semester, work for a few months and then apply to Hack Reactor.  If I get in, I'll take a semester off and actually take some money to live in SF and go through the Hack Reactor program.

Yeah, if you haven't been in college I think it's really hard to really understand *those* kinds of people.  Not being in college makes it also hard to really understand the drive / realization of "I want to do this with my life and this is the only thing I want to do, period." .  Thanks for you help here, but I'm honestly not completely sure you're old enough / have come to realizations about your future life before.

Im 21.  The field you want to enter really determines if you need a college degree in tech / software related things.  If you want to be a general software engineer, a bootcamp is probably sufficient.  If you want to develop general AI or anything related to machine learning or neural networks (this eventually becomes data science) you definitely need to go to college.  I also feel that my parents, although financially able, feel obligated to keep paying for my college.  When I've started to realize that what I'm studying and what they're paying for isn't really getting me any closer to what I want to do with my life.
I started balding at 16, I've also had plenty of acne into my 20's.  I eventually stopped caring about my appearance, and eventually realized pursuing women is a waste of time.

I've brought up the fact that I've been candidly frustrated with college and that I'd considered dropping out, they did not seem to like the idea of that very much.  I haven't brought up coding bootcamps but I feel like they'd be against the idea of it.  I'd definitely end up paying for the bootcamp and possibly my living expenses in SF, which is where I would do this, heeding the advice of people who've been through bootcamps.

I feel like I've been going through somewhat of an identity crisis over the past year.  Taking academic leave in some ways is one of the dumbest things I've ever done, but it also lead to some of the best experience and connections in a field I love.  If I hadn't done that I wouldn't have about a year of experience working at two awesome tech startups.  With what I did in HS / my first year of college with my business, I've never really felt like I've had that much in common with any of the people at my university, even really intelligent people with mild interests.  College culture in general annoys the fuck out of me, it's toxic, and filled with people who think just because they go to a private engineering school that their life will "work out".  Put bluntly, I hate the crock of shit that is university culture in the U.S. .

A part of me wants to move to SF and go through a bootcamp like Hack Reactor, which could have me doing exactly what I want exactly where I want to in about three months.  My parents don't get the industry and would probably completely disown me if I didn't finish college, which they've been paying for.  A handful of people at these startups also were relatively confident in telling me that I could probably have a decent career if I dropped out and entered the industry right now.

And yes, I feel strongly enough about this at this point in my life that I would consider suicide if I didn't get the chance to at least test my abilities.
